item.title: CGI Foundations

oerFields.estimatedDuration: One course run (6 or 15 weeks, same credits)

learningObjectives.item: Understand the fundamental principles of computer-generated imagery (CGI) and its applications
Develop proficiency in using basic 3D modeling tools and techniques
Gain knowledge of the essential elements of 3D rendering, including lighting, shading, and texturing
Learn to create and manipulate 3D assets, including characters, environments, and props
Explore the pipeline and workflow of a typical CGI project from concept to final output
Analyze the history and evolution of CGI in various industries such as film, gaming, and advertising

testOutCriteria.item: Polygonal models have good edge flow
UVs are clearly laid out and well packed
Scene is well lit using scene lights or emissive materials
B+ or better on all lecture quizzes

oerFields.whoItsFor: Everyone starting out in 3D. Take it as DART 203, or in your first run of DART 303 if you have not taken DART 203.
oerFields.author: Michael Collins

item.content:
CGI Foundations is where every DART pathway starts. You will learn how 3D images are made, from polygons to pixels, and practice each stage of the pipeline twice: once on an airline chair and once on a room. The pathway ends with a project that brings modeling, texturing, lighting and rendering together in work of your own.

After Foundations

Foundations is the prerequisite for every other pathway. On your next run of DART 303, choose a pathway that fits your interests, or explore them now to plan ahead.
